Commentary.Commentary: Now, Sri Lanka just need 14 to win the game. With 13 overs left, one would believe that the run chase will be just a formality. Let's see how many overs they will take to get to the target.

The day started with Suranga Lakmal rocking the Zimbabwe top-order with three wickets in quick succession. However, Sean Williams and Brendan Taylor then battled out with a 79-run stand. However, their wickets fell in consecutive overs and it looked like Sri Lanka might roll the hosts before they can get into the lead. But they once again found challenges from the likes of Sikandar Raza, Donald Tiripano and Regis Chakabva. But as soon as the Lankans got the second new ball, things started to happen and eventually, Kumara knocked two batsmen down quickly. Eventually, Embuldeniya took the final wicket to bundle the hosts out. Apart from de Silva, all their bowlers bagged at least a wicket with Lakmal and Kumara being the star.

That's a wrap of the Zimbabwe innings. They have managed to get just 13 runs lead which means that Sri Lanka need just 14 runs to seal the game and they have plenty of overs at their disposal to chase it down to take a 1-0 lead in the series.

He was looking to retain the strike with a single here but the ball takes the under edge and clatters into the stumps. ZIMBABWE END ON 170!

We are back for the final session of Day 5. The players are out in the middle. Regis Chakabva and Donald Tiripano will resume their batting for Zimbabwe. Dhananjaya de Silva will start the proceedings for Sri Lanka in the final session.
... Day 5, Final session ...

Now, 34 overs are remaining! The hosts need to keep battling it out. Sri Lanka need 4 wickets. They will get the chance of getting the second new ball after 7 overs in the final session, which might give them a chance of cracking things up. While there are a few balls that are keeping low, there are no demons in the surface. Zimbabwe would hope that they will manage to bat out the entire session. Join us in a while for the final session to see who stays on top at the end of it.

Another battling session of Test cricket comes to an end. It once again started with Sri Lanka getting on top with twin strikes in two overs. And, it was of the two set batters, Brendan Taylor and Sean Williams. Sikandar Raza and Regis Chakabva then combined together and played out 101 deliveries. Embuldeniya broke the stand after the Drinks break. Sri Lanka would've thought that they have a chance of running through the lower middle-order but they have once again found a challenge from the duo of Chakabva and Tiripano who are keeping the Lankans at bay.

OUT! Stumped! Yes, he has! Very sharp work from Dickwella behind the wicket. The stand is broken and Sri Lanka are once again right into the game. He has to go and with him Zimbabwe's hope of drawing this game takes a massive dive.

OUT! CAUGHT! Sean Williams, the Zimbabwe skipper departs now and half the side back in the hut. Rajitha joins the party now and Sri Lanka inching closer to victory. Back of a length ball, angling into the batter, it pitches and moves away from Sean. Williams could have left this ball alone but decides to have a poke at it. It takes the outside edge of the bat and goes to the keeper. Dickwella behind the stumps makes no mistake and takes a simple catch. The umpires want to check if this is a no ball but the replays are inconclusive as the angle of the replay is not clear. The umpires decide to stay with the on-field decision and Williams continues his walk back to the pavilion. The hosts still behind by 37 runs and have just 5 wickets in hand.

We are back for the action for the second session of Day 5. Sean Williams and Brendan Taylor make their way out to the middle. The Sri Lankan players are also making their way out to the field. Suranga Lakmal will start for the visitors.
... Day 5, Session 2 ...

The day started with Zimbabwe having all 10 wickets in hand and trailing Sri Lanka by 127 runs. The visitors started the day with a strong mindset looking to win this match and they have delivered so far as Lakmal took 3 wickets to dismiss Masvaure, Mudzinganyama and Ervine. However, after that, the stalwarts of Zimbabwe cricket, Brendan Taylor and Sean Williams took charge as they counter-attacked the Sri Lankan bowlers and are amidst a 79-run unbeaten stand. Sri Lanka could not capitalise on the start they got and the match hangs in the balance right now. The second session on Day 5 might decide the final outcome of the game. Join us at 1240 Local (1040 GMT) to find out what happens!
27 overs, 90 runs and 3 wickets have come in the morning session on Day 5 and the match is finely poised at this stage with both Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka playing well.

We are all set to begin the final day of this Test match. Prince Masvaure and Brian Mudzinganyama make their way out to the middle. The Sri Lankan players follow them out to the field. Spin to start with as Lasith Embuldeniya takes the ball. Here we go!

Pitch report - Tinotendo and Dirk Viljoen are down for the pitch report. Starts by saying that the pitch has been flat but a bit sluggish. It has not been easy to score but has been easy to survive. Adds that the ball kept low sometimes and the batsman have to be wary of that. Goes on to say that the bowlers need to pitch the ball on the full length and good length areas as cracks have opened up there and that means if the ball hits them, it might stay low. Adds there is a bit of grass on the wicket. Ends by saying the Zimbabwe batters need to be positive and they need to find a way to score runs.

After 4 days of grinding, the Test match enters its fifth day. It promises to be another exciting one where both the teams will have to grind themselves one more time to get the desired result. Sri Lanka need 10 wickets quickly. If the hosts manage to go past the lead, Sri Lanka would not want to be chasing a total which might get beyond their reach. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, would want to bat out the entire day. Who will be able to come out on top on Day 5? Let's hope we witness an intriguing final day of this Test.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

The equation is clear on Thursday, Sri Lanka need 10 wickets and Zimbabwe need to bat out the whole day. They still trail by another 127 runs but don't think that number matters. Will the Lankans force a result or is this going to end in a draw? Do join us to find out at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka batted, batted and batted, Dhananjaya got to a half ton, Dickwella too notched a half century. Mathews though was the star with a double hundred. His knock ensured the Lankans lead went above 150 before they declared. They batted long so that there is some kind of wear and tear on this wicket but for now, it still seems flat and good to bat on. The Lankans would hope that it offers some assistance for their bowlers on Day 5, whereas, the hosts would want it to be as it is.

So Zimbabwe's first challenge of getting through the last hour unscathed has been achieved! The debutant, the substitute for Kasuza, Mudzinganyama has shown great application in the middle till now. Still though one more day left and the two openers need to continue their battle.

NOT OUT! A very cheeky attempt from the keeper there. De Silva fires the first ball of his spell outside off, Mudzinganyama lets it be. Dickwella collects the ball and tries to whips the bails off. He though misses it but even if he had dislodged the bails, Brian would've been safe as he never lifted his leg. Now, as he tries to recover from his stride, he lifts his leg and Dickwella whips the bails this time and appeals. The square leg umpire refers it to the TV umpire. Replays roll in and show that Mudzinganyama planted his foot in time in the second attempt too.

Stumping appeal taken upstairs. A very late attempt from the keeper there. He tried to whip the bails in the first attempt but missed out. And as Mudzinganyama lifted his back leg, he whipped the bails off again and appealed. But the replays show that his second attempt too will not fetch him the wicket as Mudzinganyama planted his foot in time again.
